A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CGM framework. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison despite the changed title, pagination, and section numbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original GMM simulations and calibration experiments with Genie2, ESM3, TarFlow, and TinyStories-33M, including quantitative results and generated examples.

after.justification: v2 reports original simulations, protein and image experiments, and replacement Gemma-2-9B-IT experiments, including regularization sweeps and a prompting analysis.

M1.justification: v2 introduces a LoRA adaptation for calibrating Gemma, restricting updates to adapters with 110 million trainable parameters. The underlying CGM-relax and CGM-reward objectives, gradient estimators, and Algorithms 1–2 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The GMM, protein/CATH, AFHQ wildlife, and profession coverage remain. The story task gains explicit instruction-conditioned scenarios, including generation with and without a gender-parity request (Section 4.3; Figure 12). Replacing TinyStories with Gemma does not itself add a dataset.

E2.justification: The corresponding CGM comparisons retain Khalifa et al. (2021), base-model and maximum-entropy references, and protein noise/temperature controls. Shen et al. remains unevaluated. Figure 12 separately compares Gemma prompts; no additional algorithm enters the CGM comparison.

E3.justification: The language experiment switches from TinyStories-33M to Gemma-2-9B-IT with LoRA and an instruction prompt, and adds the lambda=0.01 setting. Real-model regularization grids expand. Simulation selection is also revised from minimum KL among qualifying settings to the largest lambda achieving 90% error reduction (v1 Appendix D.3; v2 Section 3).

E4.justification: v2 adds real-model regularization sensitivity studies for Genie2 and ESM3 (Figure 7) and expands TarFlow to four regularization settings (Figure 11). Figure 12 tests whether explicit gender-parity prompting resolves imbalance. These substantially extend the existing simulation sweeps and held-out-profession analysis.

E5.justification: v2 newly specifies ten iterates with two standard errors for synthetic results and three replicates with two standard errors for TarFlow; this does not establish increased runs. Language evaluation and maximum-entropy sampling repetitions change from twenty to five. Figure 12 additionally reports binomial-based standard errors.

E6.justification: Gemma results replace the TinyStories results, including revised baseline comparisons and four improved versus two worsened held-out professions. These are different-setting outcomes. Regularization and prompting results are added, and rare-event and ESM3 plot values change. TarFlow's reported lambda=10^-4 summaries change from TV 0.108/FID 21.9 to TV 0.101/FID 21.0, now with replicated-mean reporting.

T1.justification: New Appendix D.2 provides a diffusion-specific maximum-entropy proposition, endpoint-independence assumptions, and a Feynman–Kac drift characterization. Appendix C.3 adds a Fisher-information-dependent bound, corrects Proposition C.6's limit from infinity to zero, and repairs reversed concavity inequalities in C.7. The O(lambda) convergence result already existed in v1.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion extend the demonstrated model-scale claim from up to one billion to nine billion parameters, supported by the Gemma/LoRA experiment. The central contributions—two surrogate objectives for calibration across hundreds of constraints and three application domains—remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations connecting regularization error to Fisher curvature and terminal-distribution calibration to preservation of conditional diffusion paths. It also explicitly qualifies transfer to uncalibrated professions by reporting worsening cases. Existing generation-quality tradeoffs, rare-event difficulties, and tractable-likelihood limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 supplies LoRA rank, scaling, dropout, and target-layer details, discloses a 101-point uniform simulation time grid, and updates language training time from 0.1 to six hours in Table 1. The general code link remains, while the dedicated TinyStories example link is removed.

R1.justification: The existing supervised-calibration discussion moves from Appendix A into the introduction and gains references including Guo, Naeini, Lichtenstein, and Vaicenavicius. Gemma, LoRA, and classical penalty-method references are added; optimizer references are removed. The principal positioning relative to Khalifa and Shen remains.

P1.justification: Localized revisions clarify the title and gradient explanation, separate the loss relationship into Section 2.4, and regroup diffusion theory and simulation details across Appendices D/E. The language case study is rewritten for Gemma, while the overall narrative and most appendix derivations retain their structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds the conceptual diagram in Figure 1, protein sensitivity plots in Figure 7, and prompting chart in Figure 12. It expands the TarFlow display, redraws the language comparison, and revises protein plot axes. The protein and animal sample grids are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The instruction-tuned Gemma evaluation, real-model regularization sweeps, and prompting test strengthen practical validation beyond v1. Proof corrections and clearer uncertainty reporting also help. These gains are tempered by fewer language evaluation repetitions and an error in new Appendix D.2: its KL chain-rule expression combines an x(1) marginal with conditioning on x(0). Overall, the evidence and explanation improve, with remaining limitations in rigor.
